01 / FOUNDATIONS

Color roles

Usage and opacity

Each color below comes from the app. Use the role to choose a color, and the state to show what is happening.

Typography

Choose by purpose

Navigation, controls, titles, and reading text.

The homepage greeting and the optional serif article format.

Start with what the text needs to do. Each role shows where it belongs, an example from CSA, and its size, line height, and weight. Responsive variants stay together.

Role-based organization follows Material typography guidance and Carbon typography strategies. Samples use the app’s type tokens and component-specific overrides.

Surfaces

Subtle menu elevation
Dropdown
Popover
Dialog

Dropdowns and popovers share a white surface, 1 px neutral border, 8 px corners, and a 0px 4px 12px shadow at 8% opacity on desktop and 16% on mobile. Mobile dialogs and open workspace panels share New Project’s 16% backdrop and 2px blur. Other surfaces remain flat; keyboard-focus outlines remain visible.

Iconography

CSA icon library

Unselected: outlined (FILL 0). Selected: filled (FILL 1). Apply this rule to icons in selection controls, including view switches, source folders, and formatting toggles. Actions without a selected state use filled icons.

The gallery includes current and legacy app icons. Continue, Document, Source Link, Source Image, and Upload belong to older flows; Search / Find is currently hidden. Each icon shows both states and its Material Symbols name. Default glyph size is 24 px; Draft is 14 px.

Primary uses white text on Blue 600, Blue 700 on hover, and Blue 200 when disabled. Secondary (Cancel) keeps a white surface with Blue 600 text and outline, Blue 700 on hover, and Blue 200 when disabled. Tertiary uses Blue 600 text without a resting border; hover adds a Blue 700 outline and label on white. Disabled tertiary labels use Blue 200. Destructive (Delete) uses white text on Red 700, Red 800 on hover or press, and a neutral surface and label when disabled. The middle column previews hover. Keyboard focus keeps the visible shared ring.

Text contrast: Blue 600 and white measure 5.17:1; Blue 700 and white measure 6.70:1. Blue 600 text on the page canvas measures 5.02:1. All enabled and hover combinations meet the 4.5:1 normal-text AA target. Disabled states are exempt from contrast minimums.

Adaptation status segments

Switch between content to adapt and completed drafts. The selected segment uses secondary-button colors; counts show the content in each group.

Status labels use the shared detail corners (4 px). Settings chips use pill corners. Pair status color with its label and icon.

Selection fields

14 px / 600 · 36 px desktop · 46 px mobile

Format, Audience, and Voice each display their single fixed setting using the app’s shared fields and chip colors.

Toast notifications

5.5 seconds · 9 seconds with Undo
Source deleted

A white toast with dark message text, a subtle border and shadow, and an optional outlined Undo action. No icon. Standard messages dismiss after 5.5 seconds; messages with Undo dismiss after 9 seconds. Undo shows Source restored for 5.5 seconds. Show Toast Again previews the timed notification.

Content card

1 Adapted

Standard FormatGeneral AudienceUS Weekly231 Words

Pending is content added to To Adapt before a draft has been created. It starts selected, with a blue dashed border, a checkbox, its generated heading, and Format, Audience, and Voice chips. Pending content has no word count or source counter. Click its checkbox or heading to select or deselect it; Adapt 1 Content is enabled only while selected. Adapt previews the ready card and its actual word-count pill. Default and Selected preview the adapted card’s inactive and active states. Settings stay on one line with an overflow fade. The pencil opens the same red Delete menu in every state; Restore Sample returns a deleted specimen. These controls change only this reference.

04 / HANDOFF

Ready to use and maintain.

The app now reads its shared values from the same token source as this reference.

Use the system

  1. Edit dist/design-system/tokens.json.
  2. Run npm run design-system:build.
  3. Use a semantic or component CSS variable.
  4. Run npm run check and review desktop and mobile.
.primary-action {
  background: var(--csa-component-button-primary-background);
  color: var(--csa-component-button-primary-label);
  height: var(--csa-component-button-height);
  border-radius: var(--csa-component-button-radius);
}

Keep generated CSS, flat JSON, and CSV in sync. The check command detects stale exports, unresolved references, cycles, and CSS naming collisions.

Design-tool handoff

Use DTCG-compatible JSON in a token importer that supports the 2025.10 format. CSV includes slash-separated design names, resolved values, aliases, and descriptions for manual mapping.

Map colors and dimensions to variables where supported. Map typography to text styles. Check alias and composite support in your importer.

Responsive behavior

≤ 768 px
Mobile navigation, stacked canvas, 46 px selection fields, 44 px touch targets.
≥ 769 px
Desktop navigation and workspace panels.
≤ 1100 px
Editor layout adapts before the mobile navigation breakpoint.
999 / 579 px
Dashboard container widths switch to two and one columns.

Additional component-specific breakpoints: 700, 650, 480, and 370 px. CSS media and container queries retain literal values because custom properties cannot replace query thresholds.

Motion & review notes

Most interactions run 120–200 ms. Arrival uses the observed 520 ms timing and cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1). The app honors reduced-motion preferences.

The current palette is retained. Muted text on white is 2.52:1; white on primary blue is 5.17:1. Enabled button text meets the 4.5:1 AA target; muted text still needs review when used for active content.

The radius scale is standardized. Other observed values and component exceptions remain documented in the inventory.

References: DTCG Format 2025.10 · WCAG contrast minimum
